significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that the internal canary signal—“projection onto a harmfulness direction plus refusal-token confidence”—predictively declines many optimizer steps before behavioral safety collapse, and that responding to its drift velocity preserves safety at lower utility cost; this combines a form-(iii) predictive coupling with a form-(ii) conditional-control claim. It establishes a weighty phenomenon (internal deterioration temporally precedes observable failure) and a narrower mechanism (loss of harmfulness recognition is an actionable precursor), thereby fixing expectations about when collapse occurs and when an operator should intervene rather than merely reiterating the fine-tuning vulnerability documented by Qi et al., “Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To!” (ICLR 2024). The branches are determinate: lead time at or below zero and failure of gated correction would rule out this canary trajectory as an actionable precursor and undermine the proposed dynamic-control explanation, although they would not rule out other online signals. Topic substitution lowers the assessment of generic safety monitoring, but the specific “early-warning trajectory” and velocity-triggered coupling would not survive substitution with the broad LLM-safety topic, so the above-median score comes from the claim itself.

reach.justification: The concrete handles are the “canary signal,” its drift velocity, and the “drift-velocity-gated activation-anchoring intervention”; these are explicitly ex ante because they are intended to “halt or correct a run before it ships an unsafe model,” giving a fine-tuning operator an action window. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction that canary deterioration precedes behavioral collapse should transfer as an ordering and predictive coupling, but the claim does not promise transferable numerical thresholds or lead times, and it acknowledges that “directions, thresholds, and gains are model-specific.” The hypothesis ranges across benign, outlier-benign, and lightly poisoned fine-tuning and names non-researcher uptake in a “fine-tuning-as-a-service pipeline,” although its dependence on a small harmfulness canary set limits extension to uncovered safety behaviors. Under topic substitution, generic interpretability-based safety would supply neither this pre-collapse monitor nor the conditional training-time gate, so the reach score is supported by claim-specific lead time and deployment uptake rather than by the importance of LLM safety itself.
